what: Config naming lesson (2026-04-22): `recall.minScopeDepth` name is too internal-jargon. User expected "how many levels up from the file do I look" as the mental model but the implementation measures "how many fixed segments does the scope have". These two models sound similar but diverge: "levels up = 1" means different things depending on file depth (asymmetric) while "scope has N segments" is absolute. The intuitive mental model fails the core use case (mid-depth scopes like `src/api/**` reaching ALL descendants regardless of how deep) because asymmetric-distance matching can't express "scopes with ≥2 segments match anywhere under them". Keeping the absolute-specificity model, but renaming to something clearer. Options under discussion: (a) `recall.includeBroadScopes` boolean (default false — cleanest, drops the rarer "strictness>=3" tier which isn't useful); (b) `recall.scopeStrictness` with values loose/normal/strict. Lesson for future config additions: write docs/examples from the USER mental model FIRST, then see if the implementation can match. If it can't, either rename aggressively or accept that the config will need a paragraph of explanation.
why: Meta-lesson from today's config-naming confusion. Future `aide-memory` configs should be named to match user intuition even when that means hiding implementation details like "number of fixed segments in a glob." The asymmetry insight (distance-from-file is not a stable semantic, scope-specificity is) is worth preserving so future depth-like configs don't fall into the same trap.
